messages:
maria: starting an apply for feature/secret-sync, it hung after the import step. apply shows 'null_resource.import' pending forever. anyone seen this with k8s secrets + remote state?

devon: saw something like that when the import created a resource that terraform already thought existed. did you run terraform refresh first?

maria: i did a refresh, no diffs. apply output: 
```
module.k8s_secret.null_resource.import: Refreshing state... [id=123456]
module.k8s_secret.null_resource.import: Still refreshing... [10s elapsed]
module.k8s_secret.null_resource.import: Still refreshing... [20s elapsed]
^C
```

ashwin: can you paste the provider/version & backend config? sometimes an older kubernetes provider blocks on a wait_for ready condition.

maria: provider: registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/kubernetes v2.11.0, backend is s3 with dynamodb state lock.

jen: if dynamodb lock is failing you usually get a lock error. this looks like the resource refresh is hanging against k8s API. any network flakiness to cluster?

maria: cluster seemed fine, kubectl apply for other stuff worked. this resource is executing a local-exec that runs kubectl to convert a vault secret -> k8s secret during import. maybe the local-exec is blocking.

devon: ohhhhh local-exec inside import/refresh can block terraform until the command exits. check the command and timeouts. show the null_resource provisioner block?

maria: snippet from module: 
```hcl
resource "null_resource" "import" {
  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "./scripts/import-secret.sh ${var.secret_name} ${var.namespace}"
    interpreter = ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
  }
}
```

ashwin: what's in import-secret.sh? maybe it waits for a prompt or hits a missing env var and stalls.

maria: it's polling vault until secret appears, then kubectl apply. i put a long sleep/retry to be safe. hmm.

jen: that's risky. terraform runs should be idempotent but long-running shell loops can make plans hang. options: a) remove local-exec and do import as a pre-step outside terraform, b) add a timeout wrapper, or c) switch to external data source with timeout handling.

maria: i'm leaning to doing import as a pre-step in CI. this was a one-off migration i tried to do in apply.

devon: agree. quick workaround: ctrl-c and re-run after killing any stray kubectl process. also check terraform state lock in dynamodb: sometimes if apply interrupted, lock entry lingers but usually terraform notices. can you share the plan/apply command you ran?

maria: `TF_LOG=info terraform apply -auto-approve -var-file=env/prod.tfvars`

terraform-bot: Reminder: run `terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID` only if you are sure no other applies are running. See #eng-infra runbook.

ashwin: also check the script isn't waiting for STDIN. local-exec inherits stdin; if the script calls `read` for any reason it will block.

maria: confirmed the script has a debug `read -p "press enter"` in a rare codepath when secret metadata missing. facepalm.

jen: lol. fix script and re-run. if state is partially imported, you might have duplicates. best to run `terraform state list | grep k8s_secret` and `terraform import` manually if needed.

maria: will remove the read and add `--non-interactive`. doing that now, will re-run plan + apply.

devon: if you still see hanging on refresh, try `TF_PLUGIN_DISABLE_CONTROLLERS=1`? (jk) but seriously full `TF_LOG=trace` for a second run if it repeats.

maria: quick update: fixed script, re-run apply, it progresses past the import step now. one weird warning about duplicate metadata caused a recreate of 1 secret but that's expected. thanks for the quick checks! :tada:

jen: nice. file a small PR to move this import into the migration job so future runs don't hit this.

maria: yep will open PR and add a note to the runbook.

sre-bot: Created incident link: https://incidents.example.com/INC-2026 (post-mortem recommended)

maria: adding postmortem notes to the runbook now.

devon: good catch, glad it wasn't a dynamodb lock issue.

maria: thanks all :)
